description: #3927 — BRANCH differential over `list_pages_with_metadata`'s five-arm `PageSort` keyset (`keyset_for`, `src-tauri/src/commands/pages/metadata.rs`). The command had ONE query step (`pages_metadata_alphabetical`), so the ratchet read it as covered while four of its five ORDER BY / keyset arms had never run. Every step here queries the SAME three seed pages and each arm returns them in a DIFFERENT order, so each step falsifies the other four: a keyset arm wired to the wrong sort mode reddens instead of reordering invisibly. All five steps are `ordered` — a set comparison over a SORT arm proves nothing. The data is shaped so the five orders are pairwise distinct: titles Charlie/Alpha/Bravo (alphabetical), descendant counts 2/0/1 (most-content), inbound links 0/1/2 (most-linked), one op-log-bearing page (recently-modified, the other two tie at the NULL sentinel and fall to the `b.id ASC` tiebreaker), and seed id order (default). The links arrive via `edit_block` rather than the seed insert: the seed bypasses the materializer, so only an op-driven content write populates `block_links` / `pages_cache`.
name: query_pages_metadata_sorts

queries.comment: PageSort::Alphabetical -> StringAsc on COALESCE(b.content,'') COLLATE NOCASE. Title order (Alpha, Bravo, Charlie) is neither seed-id order nor any count order, so this row sequence is reachable by no other arm.
queries.name: pages_sorted_alphabetical

queries.comment: PageSort::Default -> SortKeyset::IdOnly (`b.id ASC`, no sort-key slot). Seed-label order, which every other arm permutes.
queries.name: pages_sorted_default

queries.comment: PageSort::MostContent -> I64Desc on COALESCE(pc.child_block_count, 0). Descendant counts are 2 (S1) / 0 (S2) / 1 (S3), so DESC is S1, S3, S2 — distinct from every other arm, and an ASC keyset would exactly reverse it.
queries.name: pages_sorted_most_content

queries.comment: PageSort::MostLinked -> I64Desc on COALESCE(pc.inbound_link_count, 0). S3 is linked twice (from S4 and S5), S2 once (from S6, a block on page S3 — so the count must roll a link up from the linking block to its owning page, and count the TARGET page's own subtree), S1 never.
queries.name: pages_sorted_most_linked

queries.comment: PageSort::RecentlyModified -> StringDescNullCoalesced on COALESCE((SELECT MAX(created_at) FROM op_log WHERE block_id = b.id), sentinel). Only S3 carries an op targeting the PAGE block itself (the three edit_block ops target CONTENT blocks, whose op-log rows must NOT count for their owning page), so S3 leads and the two sentinel-valued pages fall to the `b.id ASC` tiebreaker. An ASC keyset, or a sentinel that sorts above a real timestamp, puts S3 last.
queries.name: pages_sorted_recently_modified
